signature: 서술형이 **단어 세트 + 단어 수 제한**이다 (어법 지정이 아니다)
지문 둘을 [A][B] 로 묶고 표로 대조 (문항 9~10)
spec.essay_rule: 주어진 단어 전부 포함 + 단어 수 상한

essay_blueprint.조건: 완전한 한 문장 · 시제 변형 · 주어진 단어 전부 포함

materials.title: L6 본문 · Dr. Schofield
materials.text: On February 28, 1919, a man came to Dr. Schofield’s house. A man: Dr. Schofield, I have a special favor to ask you. Dr. Schofield: What can I do for you? A man: Many people are going to gather tomorrow for the independence of Korea. Could you take pictures of the event and share them with the world? At 2 p.m. on March 1, Dr. Schofield was hiding in a building and saw a large group of people gathering outside. He began to take pictures. Dr. Schofield: Unbelievable! There are so many people here. I hope the world will learn about this important event through my pictures. Do you know Seok Hopil? His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he loved his Korean name. It sounded similar to his real name, and it also had a good meaning. Dr. Schofield was a Canadian doctor, and he first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine. He wanted to teach in Korean, so he began to learn Korean right away. He studied so hard that he was able to teach in Korean after only a few years. He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement. On March 1, 1919, Dr. Schofield heard people shouting for Korean independence in Tapgol Park. He took pictures of the event with his camera. He then wrote an article about the historic event and sent it to foreign newspapers with his pictures. Dr. Schofield’s fight for Korean independence didn’t stop even after the March 1st Movement. He continued to write about the terrible situation in Korea for foreign newspapers. He was under the watchful eye of the Japanese police, so he had to go back to Canada in 1920. In 1958, he returned to Korea at the invitation of the Korean government and never left again. For the rest of his life, he worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students. Dr. Schofield died in April 1970, and he was buried in Seoul National Cemetery.

materials.title: L6 대화 ①②③
materials.text:
B: What kinds of books do you usually read?
G: I usually read sci-fi novels.
B: Then, can you recommend a good sci-fi novel for me?
G: How about The Time Machine? I think it’s the best.
G: What kinds of soft drinks do you usually have?
B: I usually drink apple soda, but today, I want to try something else. Can you recommend some new soft drinks?
G: Try a cherry soda. The cherry soda here is good.
B: OK. I’ll give it a try, then.
B: What kinds of movies do you like?
G: I like action movies. Spider-Man is my favorite.
B: Oh, I didn’t see it.
G: You didn’t? It’s really fun. I strongly recommend it.

materials.title: L5 대화 ④⑤⑥
materials.text:
B: Excuse me. I’m going to the National Art Museum. What’s the best way to get there?
G: You can walk. Go straight for about 500 meters and turn left. It’ll be on your right.
B: I see. How long will it take?
G: Only about 15 minutes.
B: Really? Thanks.
G: Excuse me, how can I get to the Dream Zoo?
B: You can take the subway.
G: I see. How long will it take?
B: I think it’ll take about 30 minutes.
B: Excuse me, how can I get to Seoul Museum from here?
G: Seoul Museum? You can get there by bus or by subway.
B: Which is faster, the bus or the subway?
G: Hmm, I think the bus is faster.
B: Really? Then, I’ll take the bus.

materials.title: T1 · 외부 지문 (밑줄 ①~⑤)
materials.text: My grandmother still keeps an old photograph of a doctor ①whom she met in the winter of 1951. At that time, her village ②used to have no hospital, so sick people had to walk for three hours to the next town. One snowy morning, she heard someone ③knocking on the front gate. It was Dr. Hall, a foreign doctor who had come to Korea with the army. He was carrying a heavy black bag ④which he filled it with medicine, and his old coat was completely covered with snow. The road was ⑤so icy that he had fallen down twice on his way to the village. He visited every house in the village that day, and my grandmother has never forgotten his tired face.

materials.title: T2 · 외부 지문 (밑줄 ①~⑤)
materials.text: Last Saturday our class visited an old train station ①which our history teacher had recommended. The guide told us that the station ②used to be full of travelers every morning in the 1960s. Now only three trains stop there each day. Inside the waiting room, we saw a large round clock ③to hang above the door. Its hands had stopped at 7:20 many years ago. The guide's voice was ④so quiet that we had to stand very close to him. Before we left, he showed us a small notebook ⑤that a young soldier had left on a bench in 1968. Nobody knows what happened to the soldier, and the notebook is still waiting for its owner.

materials.title: T3 · 외부 지문 (밑줄 ①~⑤)
materials.text: When I was ten, my father ①used to take me to the river behind our house every Saturday. The water was ②so clear that we could see small fish swimming around our feet. He taught me the names of all the trees along the bank, and I still remember the old fishing rod ③which his own father had given him. One evening I heard someone ④calling my name from the other side of the bridge. It was my father, waving both arms in the dark. Now the village is almost empty and the river is ⑤such quiet that few children ever play there, but those summer evenings still come back to me whenever it rains.

materials.title: T4 · 단문 나열
materials.text:
① I felt something cold touch my cheek.
② She is the singer whose songs I used to listen to every night.
③ There used to be a small bakery at the corner of this street.
④ The box was too heavy for me to lift it.
⑤ He was such a kind man that everyone in town trusted him.

materials.title: T5 · (A)(B)(C)
materials.text: The old house (A)[which / which it] my grandfather built with his own hands is still standing at the end of the street. On quiet nights I can hear the wooden floor (B)[to creak / creaking] under my feet. The rooms are (C)[so / such] small that only one bed fits in each of them.

materials.title: T6 · [A][B] 인물 두 편
materials.text:
[A] Edward Bell was born in England in 1872. He worked as a newspaper reporter in London, and in 1904 he came to Korea to write about the war. A year later he started his own newspaper in Seoul. He printed articles which told the world about the unfair rule of Japan. Because he was a foreigner, the Japanese police could not close his newspaper easily, though they watched him every day. He used to tell his friends, "Korea is my second home." He died in Seoul in 1909, and his grave is still in the city.

[B] Anna Shaw came to Korea from the United States in 1885. She was not a doctor but a teacher, and she opened a small school for girls in Seoul at a time when almost no girl could study. On the first day only one student came, and even she soon stopped coming. Anna did not give up. Ten years later the school had grown so large that hundreds of girls studied there. She went back to her country twice because of her health, but she always returned. She spent the rest of her life in Korea and never saw her hometown again.

materials.title: T7 · P1을 읽은 학생의 에세이
materials.text: Frank W. Schofield loved the Korean name Seok Hopil because it sounded like his real name and also had a good meaning. He first came to Korea in 1916, and he studied Korean (A)__________ that he was able to teach medicine in Korean after only a few years. On March 1, 1919, he hid in a building, watched a large group of people gathering outside, and took pictures of them. He then sent the pictures to foreign newspapers with an article. Even after that day, he kept writing about the terrible situation in Korea, and the Japanese police watched him closely. He had to leave for Canada in 1920, but in 1958 he came back (B)__________ the invitation of the Korean government and stayed here for the rest of his life.

materials.title: T8 · 배열
materials.text:
우리말: 나는 우리가 공원에서 만났던 그 소년이 노래하고 있는 것을 들었다.
[보기] we / singing / the boy / heard / whom / I / in the park / met

materials.title: T9 · 밑줄 친 so
materials.text:
① Dr. Schofield studied so hard that he could teach medicine in Korean.
② The hall was so dark that nobody could find the door.
③ He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he joined the movement.
④ There were so many people in the park that I lost my friend.
⑤ Her story was so strange that we listened to the end without saying a word.

materials.title: T10 · 대화
materials.text:
A: Excuse me, how can I get to the Seoul History Museum from here?
B: __________________________
A: Then, which is faster, the bus or the subway?
B: The subway is faster, but you have to change trains at City Hall Station.
A: I see. How long will it take?
B: About twenty minutes.
A: Thank you very much.

items.stem_ko: [P1]의 I have a special favor to ask you에서 favor의 뜻풀이로 가장 알맞은 것은?
options: something kind that you do for someone who has asked you
the feeling of liking one thing more than another one
official support or approval that a plan receives
a small present that is given to the guests at a party
an advantage that makes it easier for you to win
items.why_ko: favor는 다의어로, 여기서는 '부탁·호의(남을 위해 해 주는 친절한 행동)'의 뜻이다. ②는 in favor of/선호, ③은 지지·승인, ④는 party favor, ⑤는 유리한 점으로 모두 다른 뜻이다.

items.stem_ko:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말로, [P1]에 쓰인 것은?

: a series of actions by a group of people who share the same aim and work together to achieve it
items.why_ko: '같은 목표를 위해 함께 행동하는 사람들의 운동'은 movement이며, [P1]의 the Korean independence movement에 쓰였다. government, gathering도 본문에 보이지만 뜻풀이와 맞지 않는다.

items.stem_ko: [P1]에 쓰인 낱말과 그 뜻풀이가 잘못 짝지어진 것은?
options: favor – something kind that you do for another person
sound – to seem to be a particular thing when you hear it
article – a piece of writing about one subject in a newspaper
cemetery – an area of land where dead people are buried
right – the side of your body that is opposite the left
items.why_ko: [P1]의 the right to be independent에서 right는 '권리(something you are allowed to have or do)'라는 뜻이다. ⑤의 풀이는 '오른쪽'이라는 다른 뜻이므로 본문 쓰임과 맞지 않는다.

options: Summer Evenings by the River That I Still Miss
How to Catch River Fish with an Old Fishing Rod
The Danger of Swimming in a Deep Country River
A New Bridge That Completely Changed My Village
Why Children Today Are Afraid of the Countryside
items.why_ko: 글쓴이는 아버지와 강가에서 보낸 어린 시절의 저녁을 그리워하며 회상하고 있다. ⑤는 '아이들이 거의 놀지 않는다'는 한 구절만 확대한 함정이고, ②③④는 글의 소재만 빌린 오답이다.

options: Why did Dr. Schofield like his Korean name so much?
When and for what purpose did he first come to Korea?
How many pictures did he take in Tapgol Park that day?
Why did he have to leave Korea and go back to Canada?
Where was he buried after he died in April 1970?
items.why_ko: 사진을 찍었다는 사실은 나오지만 몇 장을 찍었는지는 언급이 없다. ①은 이름이 실제 이름과 비슷하고 좋은 뜻이어서, ②는 1916년 의학을 가르치러, ④는 일본 경찰의 감시 때문에, ⑤는 서울 국립묘지로 각각 답할 수 있다.

options: Dr. Schofield learned Korean in Canada before he came to Korea in 1916.
The man who visited him asked him to gather people for the March 1st Movement.
He sent his article and pictures to Korean newspapers right after the event.
He came back to Korea in 1958 and stayed there until the end of his life.
After going back to Canada in 1920, he stopped writing about Korea.
items.why_ko: 1958년 한국 정부의 초청으로 돌아와 다시는 떠나지 않았다고 했다. ①은 한국에 와서 배우기 시작했고, ②는 사람들을 모아 달라가 아니라 사진을 찍어 달라는 부탁이었으며, ③은 외국 신문사, ⑤는 3·1 운동 뒤에도 계속 기사를 썼다는 내용과 어긋난다.

items.stem_ko: [P1]의 He was under the watchful eye of the Japanese police가 의미하는 바로 가장 알맞은 것은?
options: 그는 일본 경찰의 보호를 받으며 활동했다.
그는 일본 경찰의 감시를 받고 있었다.
그는 일본 경찰의 눈을 피해 몸을 숨기고 있었다.
그는 일본 경찰의 허가를 받아 취재를 계속했다.
items.why_ko: watchful eye는 '감시하는 눈길'이므로 감시를 받고 있었다는 뜻이며, 그래서 1920년에 캐나다로 돌아가야 했다. ④는 3월 1일 건물에 숨어 있었다는 앞 내용과 섞은 함정이다.

options: The girl who usually reads sci-fi novels says The Time Machine is the best one.
The boy usually drinks apple soda, but he decides to try a cherry soda.
The girl strongly recommends Spider-Man, which the boy has not seen yet.
The boy going to the National Art Museum is told that it takes only about 15 minutes on foot.
The girl asking about the Dream Zoo decides to walk because it takes only 30 minutes.
items.why_ko: Dream Zoo에 대해서는 지하철을 타라는 안내를 받았고 약 30분이 걸린다고 했을 뿐, 걸어가겠다고 한 말은 없다. 나머지는 모두 대화 내용과 일치한다.

items.stem_ko: [T6]의 [A], [B]를 정리한 다음 표의 ①~⑤ 중, 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
options: 한국에서 한 일 — [A] 일본의 통치를 비판하는 기사를 씀 / [B] 여학생을 위한 병원을 세움
말년 — [A] 1909년 서울에서 사망 / [B] 한국에서 여생을 보냄
items.why_ko: [B]의 Anna Shaw는 병원이 아니라 여학생을 위한 작은 '학교'를 열었다. 나머지 항목은 두 글의 내용과 모두 일치한다.

options: [A]는 한국에 오기 전부터 서울에서 자신의 신문을 운영하고 있었다.
[B]가 세운 학교에는 개교 첫날부터 수백 명의 학생이 모였다.
[A]는 일본 경찰에게 신문사를 빼앗기고 영국으로 돌아갔다.
[B]는 건강 때문에 고국으로 돌아간 뒤 다시는 한국에 오지 않았다.
두 사람은 모두 한국에서 생의 마지막 시기를 보냈다.
items.why_ko: [A]는 1909년 서울에서 사망했고 [B]는 한국에서 여생을 보냈다. ①은 한국에 온 이듬해에 신문을 창간했고, ②는 첫날 단 한 명, ③은 외국인이라 쉽게 폐간되지 않았다고 했으며, ④는 두 번 돌아갔다가 항상 다시 왔다.

items.stem_ko: [T1]의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.why_ko: 목적격 관계대명사 which가 filled의 목적어 역할을 하므로 뒤에 다시 목적어 it을 쓸 수 없다(which he filled with medicine). ①은 met의 목적어 자리의 whom, ②는 과거의 상태를 나타내는 used to+동사원형, ③은 지각동사 heard의 목적격보어 현재분사, ⑤는 so+형용사+that 구문으로 모두 옳다.

items.stem_ko: [T10]의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
options: You can walk there in about fifteen minutes.
You can get there by bus or by subway.
I'm going there, too. Let's take a taxi together.
The bus is much faster than the subway.
You'd better not take the subway at this time.
items.why_ko: 바로 뒤에서 A가 '버스와 지하철 중 어느 것이 더 빠른가'를 묻고 있으므로 두 교통수단을 함께 알려 주는 말이 들어가야 한다. ④는 뒤에서 B가 지하철이 더 빠르다고 한 말과 모순되고, ①③⑤는 이어지는 질문과 연결되지 않는다.
too ~ to부정사 구문에서 to부정사의 목적어가 문장의 주어(The box)와 같으므로 뒤에 it을 다시 쓸 수 없다(to lift). ①은 지각동사 felt+원형부정사, ②는 소유격 관계대명사, ③은 There used to be, ⑤는 such a+형용사+명사+that 구문으로 모두 옳다.

items.stem_ko: [T7]은 [P1]을 읽은 학생이 쓴 에세이이다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.why_ko: (A)는 '너무 ~해서 …하다'의 so+부사+that 구문이므로 so hard, (B)는 '~의 초청으로'를 뜻하는 굳어진 전치사 결합 at the invitation of이다. too ~ that은 쓸 수 없고, such는 명사를 꾸미며, hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 뜻이라 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

items.stem_ko: [T2]의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.why_ko: 지각동사 saw의 목적격보어로는 원형부정사나 현재분사를 쓰므로 to hang이 아니라 hanging(또는 hang)이 되어야 한다. ①⑤는 목적격 관계대명사, ②는 '예전에는 ~이었다'의 used to be, ④는 so+형용사+that 구문으로 옳다.

items.stem_ko: [T5]의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현끼리 바르게 짝지은 것은?
items.why_ko: (A) built의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사 which 뒤에는 목적어 it을 다시 쓰지 않는다. (B) 지각동사 hear의 목적격보어는 원형부정사나 현재분사이므로 creaking. (C) 뒤에 형용사 small이 오므로 so ~ that이다(such 뒤에는 명사구가 온다).

items.stem_ko: [T9]의 밑줄 친 so의 쓰임이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
items.why_ko: ③의 so는 '그래서'라는 결과를 나타내는 접속사이고, 나머지는 모두 so+형용사/부사(+명사)+that 구문에서 정도를 나타내는 부사 so이다.

items.stem_ko: [T3]의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.why_ko: 뒤에 형용사 quiet가 오므로 such가 아니라 so quiet that이 되어야 한다(such는 「such+a(n)+형용사+명사」 형태로 쓴다). ①은 과거의 습관 used to+동사원형, ②는 so ~ that, ③은 given의 목적어 자리의 목적격 관계대명사, ④는 지각동사 heard의 목적격보어 현재분사로 옳다.

items.stem_ko: [T8]의 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [보기]의 말을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 배열할 때, 여섯 번째로 오는 것은?
items.why_ko: I / heard / the boy / whom / we / met / in the park / singing 의 순서이므로 여섯 번째는 met이다. 지각동사 heard의 목적어 the boy를 목적격 관계대명사절이 수식하고, 목적격보어 singing이 맨 뒤에 온다.

essays.prompt_ko:
[P1]의 내용과 일치하도록, [보기]의 말을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완전한 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
<조건> ① 필요하면 시제와 어형을 바꿀 것 ② 목적격 관계대명사가 반드시 들어가도록 할 것 ③ [보기] 외의 단어는 추가하지 말 것 (단어 수 제한 없음)
essays.answer_en: Dr. Schofield sent the article which he wrote to foreign newspapers.
essays.why_ko: send→sent, write→wrote로 과거시제로 바꾸고, wrote의 목적어 자리에 목적격 관계대명사 which를 써서 the article을 수식해야 한다. 관계대명사절 안에 it을 다시 쓰면 감점이다.

essays.prompt_ko:
길을 묻는 친구에게 "지하철로 가서 Anguk역에서 내려."라고 안내하는 말을 영어 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
<조건> ① [보기]의 말을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것 ② 알맞은 전치사 두 개를 넣을 것 ③ Go로 시작하고 9단어 이하로 쓸 것
essays.target_grammar: 교통수단 by + 하차 get off at
essays.answer_en: Go by subway and get off at Anguk Station.
essays.why_ko: 교통수단 앞에는 관사 없이 by subway를 쓰고, '~역에서 내리다'는 get off at ~ Station으로 굳어진 결합이다. 총 9단어로 조건에 맞는다.

essays.prompt_ko:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 영작하시오.

날씨가 너무 추워서 우리는 안에 머물렀다.
<조건> ① [보기]의 말을 모두 사용하되 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 것 ② so ~ that 구문을 사용할 것 ③ It으로 시작하여 8단어 이하로 쓸 것
essays.answer_en: It was so cold that we stayed inside.
essays.why_ko: 날씨는 비인칭 주어 It으로 받아야 8단어를 넘지 않는다(The weather was ~로 쓰면 9단어가 되어 조건 위반). stay는 과거형 stayed로 바꾸고 so cold that 구문을 쓴다.

essays.prompt_ko:
다음 질문에 대한 답을 [P1]에서 찾아, 본문에 있는 단어만 사용하여 정확히 네 단어로 쓰시오. (어형을 바꾸거나 단어를 추가하지 말 것)

Q: What did Dr. Schofield hear people doing in Tapgol Park on March 1, 1919?
essays.why_ko: 본문의 heard people shouting for Korean independence에서 지각동사의 목적격보어인 현재분사구를 그대로 옮겨 쓰면 된다. shout, shouted 등으로 어형을 바꾸면 안 된다.
